guide.title: Steakhouses in Miami: Sixteen Rooms Across Four Cities
guide.intro: Sixteen rooms, and they are spread across four separate municipalities rather than one. Seven stand in the City of Miami: three in Brickell on South Miami Avenue and Brickell Avenue, one in the Design District, one on Calle Ocho in Little Havana, one on Northeast Second Avenue north of the Design District, and one under a banyan tree in Little River. Six more are in Miami Beach, four of them within a few blocks of South of Fifth on First Street, Washington Avenue and Ocean Drive, with two further up Collins. Coral Gables holds two on Ponce de Leon and San Ignacio, and Aventura holds one on West Country Club Drive. This is one page because Greater Miami's own tourism board publishes one steakhouse list across all four.

sections.heading: Miami proper: Brickell, the Design District and the corridors north
sections.body:
Seven rooms inside the City of Miami, and no two of them are the same kind of steakhouse.

Brickell has three. Fleming's is at 600 Brickell Avenue, Suite 150, a block from Brickell City Centre, with seven steak cuts on the dinner list. Dirty French Steakhouse is at 1200 Brickell Avenue, all mirrored walls and animal print, running filet mignon and a wagyu tomahawk. Baires Grill is at 1010 South Miami Avenue, an Argentine steakhouse with four sister rooms in Coral Gables, Doral, Miami Beach and Sunny Isles.

COTE is at 3900 Northeast Second Avenue in the Design District: a Korean steakhouse with a Michelin star, smokeless grills set into the tables, a dry-aging room, USDA prime dry-aged beef and a steak omakase under executive chef David Shim. The tourism board's own description is that it fuses the ritual of Korean barbecue with the polish of a classic American steakhouse, and that is exactly the genre this survey admits.

The last three go by neighborhood rather than by corridor. El Toro Loco is at 1970 Southwest Eighth Street, the Calle Ocho room in Little Havana, cooking USDA Prime over open fire with a Mediterranean turn and a butcher shop attached; the operator runs five more rooms across Miami-Dade. Fiorito is at 5555 Northeast Second Avenue, a small family-run Argentine parrilla whose ribeye and churrasco come out with chimichurri. Sunny's Steakhouse is up in Little River on Northwest Miami Court, an indoor-outdoor room built around a banyan tree.

sections.heading: Miami Beach and South of Fifth
sections.body:
Six rooms in a separate city, and four of them are inside a few blocks of each other at the southern tip.

Prime 112 is at 112 Ocean Drive, the South of Fifth room that dry-aged prime beef in this town more or less starts with; it belongs to the Myles group, alongside Prime Italian, Prime Fish and Big Pink. Papi Steak is round the corner at 736 First Street, created by David Einhorn and David Grutman, with velvet booths, tomahawk presentations carried through the room, and beef hand-selected and aged in the operator's own climate-controlled facilities. Fogo de Chão holds 836 First Street, a churrascaria where Brazilian-trained gaucho chefs carve fire-roasted meats at the table off a market table of salads, cured meats and imported cheeses. Smith & Wollensky is at 1 Washington Avenue in South Pointe Park, recently renovated, working USDA Prime dry-aged beef with a second-story Overlook Deck over the bay.

Two more sit up Collins Avenue. Los Fuegos is at 3201 Collins inside the Faena, Francis Mallmann's Argentine room, with an open-fire kitchen doing asado and wood-fired meats among leopard-print booths and red cushions. STK South Beach is at 2305 Collins inside the 1 Hotel, a steakhouse run as a lounge, with New York strip and wagyu on the list.

sections.heading: Coral Gables and Aventura
sections.body:
Three rooms in two more municipalities, twenty miles apart.

Coral Gables has the longest-running address on the page. Christy's is at 3101 Ponce de Leon Boulevard and has been trading since 1978, according to the restaurant's own history, with filet mignon at six, eight and ten ounces and small dining rooms hung with artwork. Daniel's Miami is at 1500 San Ignacio Avenue, sister to the Michelin-recommended Daniel's in Fort Lauderdale, running grilled prime cuts with a separate bar room beside the dining room.

Aventura has one: Bourbon Steak, at 19999 West Country Club Drive. It is Michael Mina's Florida steakhouse, with mirrored glass and gilded finishes, Japanese A5 and American wagyu cooked over wood, and a wine program running past eight hundred and fifty selections. Mina's other Bourbon Steak on this site's steakhouse pages is in Georgetown, Washington, and the two rooms are separate places on separate guides.

faq.question: Why is Miami Beach on a page called Miami?
faq.answer: Because Miami proper sustains a page on its own and the beach rooms belong with it. Seven of the sixteen stand inside the City of Miami — enough for a page without borrowing — and the four-city spread is how Greater Miami's own tourism board publishes its steakhouse list, which runs from Little River and Little Havana through the Design District and Brickell out to South Beach, Coral Gables and Aventura. Every room here is filed under the city it actually stands in, so the Miami Beach rooms carry Miami Beach and the Coral Gables rooms carry Coral Gables, even though the guide sits on Miami.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. That breadth is not a loophole in Miami, it is the city: without it the page would lose a churrascaria, two Argentine parrillas and a Korean steakhouse with a Michelin star, and would describe a different town than the one that exists. What it excludes is a restaurant that merely serves a good steak, however famous the steak.

faq.question: Which rooms did this survey check and leave off?
faq.answer: Four. Ocean Prime's own locations list has no Miami room at all — the Florida entries are Fort Lauderdale, Naples, Orlando, Sarasota and Tampa. Meat Market's own site lists Tampa, Palm Beach, Boca Raton and Puerto Rico, with no Lincoln Road room. Red South Beach's web address no longer belongs to the restaurant. And Los Ranchos, the Nicaraguan churrasco house the survey found at Bayside, now lists only Coral Gables and The Falls, neither of them the room that was scoped. A room whose status cannot be verified is left off rather than published with a hedge.

faq.question: Is COTE Miami the same restaurant as COTE in New York?
faq.answer: Same operator, different room. The Manhattan COTE is on West 22nd Street in the Flatiron District and is published on this site by the neighborhood guide that already carries it; the Miami room at 3900 Northeast Second Avenue in the Design District is its own place, with its own Michelin star, its own dry-aging room and its own chef. Both qualify for a steakhouse survey on the same ground: a Korean-style beef room is one of the genres the inclusion rule names.

faq.question: Where are the dry-aging rooms?
faq.answer: Three of the sixteen say so plainly. COTE keeps a dry-aging room off the Design District dining room and serves USDA prime dry-aged beef. Smith & Wollensky works USDA Prime dry-aged beef at South Pointe. Papi Steak ages its beef in the operator's own climate-controlled facilities. Prime 112's dry-aged prime beef is what the tourism board leads with when it describes the room. None of the four publishes how long, so this page does not say.

photos.title: Brickell Avenue, Miami
photos.description: Looking up from the roadway at two office towers on Brickell Avenue: a blue-glass block lettered TRUIST at its parapet in front, and behind it a taller tower banded in stone and glass with BANK OF AMERICA across its upper corner. Palms, traffic signals on a gray mast and a red awning line the sidewalk below, parked cars stand at the curb on the right, and the sky is cloudless.
photos.author: Phillip Pessar

places.name: Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar
places.summary: Fleming's Brickell room is at 600 Brickell Avenue, Suite 150, one block from Brickell City Centre. Seven steak cuts run the dinner menu, with seafood and plant-based dishes behind them and outdoor seating on the street.

places.name: Dirty French Steakhouse
places.summary: Dirty French Steakhouse holds 1200 Brickell Avenue, a room of mirrored walls and bold animal prints. Filet mignon and a wagyu tomahawk are the cuts the house leads with.

places.name: Baires Grill Brickell
places.summary: Baires Grill's Brickell parrilla is at 1010 South Miami Avenue, serving Argentine cuts and homemade Argentine dishes with sidewalk seating. The operator runs four more rooms, in Coral Gables, Doral, Miami Beach and Sunny Isles.

places.name: COTE Miami
places.summary: COTE Miami is the Design District's Korean steakhouse, at 3900 Northeast Second Avenue, with smokeless grills set into every table, a dry-aging room off the dining room and USDA prime dry-aged beef. Executive chef David Shim runs a steak omakase alongside the à la carte list, and the room holds a Michelin star.

places.name: El Toro Loco Steakhouse
places.summary: The Calle Ocho steakhouse in Little Havana, at 1970 Southwest Eighth Street, cooking generous USDA Prime beef over open fire with a Mediterranean turn and a butcher shop selling the same raw cuts. Five more El Toro Loco rooms run across Miami-Dade.

places.name: Fiorito
places.summary: Fiorito is a small family-run Argentine parrilla at 5555 Northeast Second Avenue, working certified Angus beef in classic cuts — ribeye and churrasco with chimichurri — alongside a short list of Italian and Spanish dishes.

places.name: Sunny's Steakhouse
places.summary: Sunny's Steakhouse is in Little River, an airy indoor-outdoor steak room anchored by a sprawling banyan tree rather than by a formal dining room.

places.name: Prime 112
places.summary: Prime 112 holds 112 Ocean Drive in South of Fifth, and dry-aged prime beef is what the room is known for. It belongs to the Myles Restaurant Group, which also runs Prime Italian, Prime Fish and Big Pink nearby.

places.name: Papi Steak
places.summary: Papi Steak is at 736 First Street in South of Fifth, created by David Einhorn and David Grutman, with velvet booths and a tomahawk carried through the room as a presentation. Every cut of beef is hand-selected and aged in the operator's own climate-controlled facilities, and the group's other room is in Las Vegas.

places.name: Fogo de Chão
places.summary: The South Beach churrascaria at 836 First Street, where Brazilian-trained gaucho chefs carve fire-roasted steak, lamb, chicken and pork at the table. A market table of salads, fresh-cut vegetables, cured meats, smoked salmon and imported cheeses runs alongside the meat.

places.name: Smith & Wollensky
places.summary: Smith & Wollensky sits at 1 Washington Avenue in South Pointe Park, at the southern tip of Miami Beach, working USDA Prime dry-aged beef. A recent renovation added a second-story Overlook Deck looking over the bay and the downtown skyline.

places.name: Los Fuegos at Faena
places.summary: Francis Mallmann's Argentine room inside the Faena at 3201 Collins Avenue, built around an open-fire kitchen doing asado and wood-fired meats. Leopard-print booths and red-cushioned seats run through it, and the room is Michelin Recommended.

places.name: STK South Beach
places.summary: STK's South Beach steakhouse is inside the 1 Hotel at 2305 Collins Avenue, a dining room run as a lounge with crocodile tiles and a DJ. New York strip and wagyu carry the beef list.

places.name: Christy's
places.address: 3101 Ponce De Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL 33134
places.summary: Christy's is a classic steakhouse at 3101 Ponce de Leon Boulevard in Coral Gables, trading since 1978 according to the restaurant's own history and a local landmark for over forty years. Filet mignon comes at six, eight and ten ounces, in small dining rooms hung with artwork.

places.name: Daniel's Miami
places.address: 1500 San Ignacio Ave, Coral Gables, FL 33146
places.summary: Daniel's Miami is an upscale steakhouse at 1500 San Ignacio Avenue in Coral Gables, sister to the Michelin-recommended Daniel's in Fort Lauderdale. Grilled prime cuts lead the menu, with local seafood and Italian dishes behind them and a separate bar room alongside.

places.name: Bourbon Steak
places.address: 19999 W Country Club Dr, Aventura, FL 33180
places.summary: Michael Mina's Florida steakhouse is at 19999 West Country Club Drive in Aventura, a room of mirrored glass and gilded finishes. Japanese A5 and American wagyu are cooked over wood, and the wine list runs past eight hundred and fifty selections with nightly sommelier-guided tastings.

entries.name: Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar
entries.note: 600 Brickell Avenue, a block from Brickell City Centre. Seven cuts on the dinner list and a wine bar attached.

entries.name: Dirty French Steakhouse
entries.note: 1200 Brickell Avenue. The wagyu tomahawk is the order, and the room is built to be looked at.

entries.name: Baires Grill Brickell
entries.note: 1010 South Miami Avenue. Argentine cuts and empanadas; four sister rooms across the county.

entries.name: COTE Miami
entries.note: 3900 NE Second Avenue, Design District. Book the steak omakase and let the grill in the table do the work.

entries.name: El Toro Loco Steakhouse
entries.note: 1970 SW Eighth Street, Little Havana. Buy the same raw beef at the butcher counter on the way out.

entries.name: Fiorito
entries.note: 5555 NE Second Avenue. A family parrilla; the churrasco with chimichurri is the plate to get.

entries.name: Sunny's Steakhouse
entries.note: Northwest Miami Court, Little River. Sit under the banyan tree rather than inside.

entries.name: Prime 112
entries.note: 112 Ocean Drive, South of Fifth. The dry-aged prime beef room the neighborhood was built around.

entries.name: Papi Steak
entries.note: 736 First Street. The tomahawk arrives as a piece of theater, in a briefcase.

entries.name: Fogo de Chão
entries.note: 836 First Street. Rodizio service — the gaucho chefs keep coming until the card turns red.

entries.name: Smith & Wollensky
entries.note: 1 Washington Avenue, South Pointe Park. Ask for the Overlook Deck upstairs.

entries.name: Los Fuegos at Faena
entries.note: 3201 Collins Avenue. Mallmann's fires, and the asado is the reason to book.

entries.name: STK South Beach
entries.note: 2305 Collins Avenue, in the 1 Hotel. Loud, late, and the strip steak holds up anyway.

entries.name: Christy's
entries.note: 3101 Ponce de Leon Boulevard. The oldest room on this page, per its own history, and it still serves the Caesar tableside.

entries.name: Daniel's Miami
entries.note: 1500 San Ignacio Avenue. The bar room takes walk-ins when the dining room is full.

entries.name: Bourbon Steak
entries.note: 19999 West Country Club Drive, Aventura. Wood-grilled wagyu, and a sommelier who will walk the list with you.

links.note: COTE's Manhattan room, at 16 West 22nd Street, is published by the Flatiron District guide. The Design District room here is a separate restaurant under the same operator.
